- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent price is falling.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops from 68+ to 62–64), model often fails to correct; apply a “reversion bias” rule: if forecast > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15%.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment lag: if sentiment drops sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish reversal” (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.6), model often misreads trend; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
